EU citizens will not be required to obtain a work authorisation or a residence permit for employment. For stays of up to 90 days, they may carry out lawful activities on the territory of the Republic of Moldova without additional formalities.

For a stay exceeding 90 days, EU citizens will have to obtain a residence card, issued by the General Inspectorate for Migration (IGM), which is not conditional on a particular purpose of stay. The residence card is granted for up to 5 years and gives the holder the right to carry out any lawful activity, while guaranteeing the rights and obligations provided by national law.

Examining the legal framework and social policies of the RM applicable to the employment of foreigners, we found that this part of the RM's legislation is a modest one.

So, on the basis of the acts mentioned, we found that the RM promotes a partnership policy in the labour field with the aim of placing foreigners in the Moldovan labour market because of the insufficiency of domestic human resources needed to fill vacant jobs, in particular those requiring high qualification.

Likewise, following study of the legislative aspect concerning employment in the RM, we found that the main law establishing the employment procedure is Law of the RM No. 180 of 10.07.2008 on labour migration.

Following the study carried out, we can state with certainty that obtaining the right of temporary residence for work by the foreign citizen in the territory of the RM is the main legal task of both the foreign employee and the employer in the RM.

Therefore, the legal framework governing the grant of the right of residence for work to a foreign citizen in the territory of the RM is set by: Law of the RM No. 200 of 16.07.2010 on the regime of foreigners in the RM and Government Decision No. 115 of 31.01.2018 approving the List of priority occupations, the latter act providing a number of facilities for foreign employees where their professional qualification is included in the list in that decision.

The grant of the right of temporary residence for work to the foreign citizen is guaranteed by the provisions of the Constitution of the RM, which allows the employment of foreign citizens with the full range of rights and obligations, as in the case of domestic employees, with some exceptions established for stateless persons.
The list of documents required of the foreign citizen for employment in the Moldovan labour market is an exhaustive one.

In addition, under Art. 141 of Law of the RM No. 180 of 10.07.2008 on labour migration, for examination of the application for granting or extending the right to work, the requesting beneficiary pays the state fee in the amount set by Law of the RM No. 1216 of 03.12.1992 on state fees, which exempts the foreign citizen from additional costs related to employment, by Law of the RM No. 452 of 28.12.2023.

In this vein, we note that from a legal point of view such a legal provision is an ineffective one, which at the very least must be replaced by the Moldovan legislator, because how can the foreign citizen, being in his country of origin, read the local newspapers of the RM in which job offers are presented!?

In this way, we put forward a de lege ferenda proposal under which Art. 7(1)(a) of Law of the RM No. 180 of 10.07.2008 would be amended to read: "Copy of the job advertisement published in the media and on specialised portals (websites, government platforms and other information domains), giving information on the number and offer of vacant jobs".

Thus, in this regard we put forward a new de lege ferenda proposal for an addition, under which we find it necessary that a checklist of the proposed working conditions, with photos or even video material of the workplace offered by the employer in the RM, be annexed to the draft individual employment contract intended to be concluded with the foreign employee.

Comparing Moldovan labour legislation with Romanian and European legislation, we find in no domestic act in the field a definition of the employment relationship with a foreign element, which is why we put forward a de lege ferenda proposal: that a framework law be drawn up covering the main aspects of the individual employment contract to which a foreign citizen is a party.

The content of such an employment contract is largely dictated not by the Labour Code of the RM, as usual, but by the provisions of Law of the RM No. 180 of 10.07.2008 on labour migration, in particular by the provisions of its Annex No. 1.

In this respect, neither the Labour Code of the RM nor other legislative acts applicable to the employment of foreigners prohibit concluding individual employment contracts of indefinite duration with foreign citizens.

But if we refer to the duration of the right of temporary residence granted to the foreign citizen for work, which is given for a period of one year under Law of the RM No. 180 of 10.07.2008 on labour migration, we consider that this contract must be included among limited ones, that is, concluded for a fixed term.

In the same practical respect, based on the legal rules applicable to labour migration and the employment of foreigners, we consider that in the RM such a procedure is nevertheless particularly bureaucratic.

Thus, we consider that, once all procedures are moved to digital mode, such a burden should be solved by creating a digital form to be completed by the Moldovan employer;

If we analyse the list proposed by our legislator, defining the professions needed by domestic employers, we again find serious blunders, we believe because the professions defined are generalised.

Free data: data held by public participants are made available to other public participants free of charge. Data held by public participants are made available to private participants for a fee in the cases provided by law and on the basis of the mechanism set by the Government;

Data availability: data held by participants in the data exchange are equally available to any other participant on the basis of its legal mandate, while ensuring legal, organisational, semantic and technical interoperability requirements. Participants in the data exchange are obliged to ensure the availability of all data sets they hold;

Legality of data exchange: data held by participants are provided through the interoperability platform to another participant where that participant invokes a purpose and a legal basis for processing the requested data set and complies with the security and confidentiality requirements arising from the legal regime of the data concerned;

Authenticity of data: data from participants' information systems provided through the interoperability platform are presumed authentic, considered complete and truthful and form the basis of legal acts, and data providers are obliged to ensure their integrity and truthfulness;
Shared responsibility: each participant in the data exchange is responsible, according to its role in the data exchange process, for its part of the process.
